models_evaluated: CBCT AI diagnosis with internal denoising module (model-agnostic)
baseline AI diagnosis model without denoising

links.outcome: Human reader diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: Human diagnosis accuracy improved by 11% (from 71.7 to 83.0%) with the proposed method; AI accuracy rose from 73.4 to 83.0% vs baseline. Overreliance not assessed.
links.quote: The external validation results for the unified diagnosis of sinus fungal ball, chronic rhinosinusitis, and normal cases show that the proposed method improves the micro-, macro-average area under the curve, and accuracy by 7.4, 5.6, and 9.6% (from 86.2, 87.0, and 73.4 to 93.6, 92.6, and 83.0%), respectively, compared with a baseline while improving human diagnosis accuracy by 11% (from 71.7 to 83.0%), demonstrating technical differentiation and clinical effectiveness.

unlisted_practices: Internal denoising module before diagnosis to improve AI diagnostic performance on noisy CBCT images

screen.reason: Evaluates an AI-based denoising and diagnostic system on CBCT scans and measures impact on human reader accuracy in an external validation reader study, but it evaluates a novel model pipeline rather than an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
